 Judgment

Both these appeals are arising out of judgment and award dated 11th June, 2020 passed in MVC No.472 and 473 of 2019 by the Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal- III,
Hagaribommanahalli (hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal" for brevity).

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal- III,
Hagaribommanahalli
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties in these appeals are referred to their status and rank before the Tribunal.

3. The facts of the case in brief are that, on 13th March, 2018, petitioner-claimants were going to their native Yenigi from Hadagali on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 35/EH-3669 and when they reached Hampasagara-3 near Bannikallu cross, the driver of car bearing Registration No.KA- 26/M-5906 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the backside of the motorcycle on which the petitioners were proceeding, and as a result, the petitioners fell and sustained grievous injuries.

It is further stated as to the injuries sustained by the petitioners in the accident and also as to pain and agony, medical expenses incurred, loss of future earning NC: 2023:KHC-D:9031-DB due to accidental injuries etc., and accordingly sought for compensation.

4. Pursuant to service of notice, Respondents 2 and 3 in both cases appeared through their counsel;
Respondent No.1 placed ex-parte.

Respondent No.2 appeared through his power of attorney and filed her written statement, wherein it is stated that respondent No.1 was having valid driving licence and the accident caused due to negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle who rode the same without headgear and in a negligent manner dashed against the car.
The offending vehicle has been insured with respondent No.3.
Further, it is denied as to the averments made in the claim petitions and sought for dismissal of the same.
5. Respondent No.3-Insurance Company filed its written statement contending that the petitions are not maintainable in law and also on facts.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle which came on the wrong side and dashed against the car.
The driver of the car had no valid and effective driving licence at the relevant point of time and hence violated the policy conditions.

It is NC: 2023:KHC-D:9031-DB further contended that the liability, if any, depends upon the validity of Registration Certificate, Fitness Certificate and terms and conditions of the policy and further denied as to the other averments made in claim petitions as false and accordingly,
sought for dismissal of claim petitions.

In support of his submission, the learned counsel relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of KAJAL v. JAGDISH CHAND reported in (2020)4 SCC 413 and the decision of this Court in Miscellaneous First Appeal No.689 of 2018 and connected appeals.

entities.text: KAJAL v. JAGDISH CHAND reported in (2020)4 SCC 413
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the following issues in both the petitions:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 13.03.2018 near Bannikallu cross, Hampasagara-3, H.B.Halli is due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-26/M-5906?

sentences.text: 4 2. Whether the 3rd respondent/Insurance Company proves that the 1st respondent driver of the NC: 2023:KHC-D:9031-DB offending vehicle did not possess valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and thereby he has violated the policy conditions?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order or award?

7. In order to prove the case of the petitioners, two witness were examined as PWs1 and 2 and, in all,
74 documents were got marked as Exhibits P1 to P74.
The treated Doctor has been examined as PW3.
Respondents have not adduced any evidence on their behalf, but the copy of the Insurance Policy is marked as Exhibit R1.

In view of the above finding, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petitions and awarded compensation of Rs.10,78,248/- in MVC No.472 of 2019 and Rs.4,23,511/- in MVC No.473 of 2019 with interest at 8% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded, the appellant-claimants are before this Court in these appeals seeking enhancement of compensation.

9. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners in both cases, submit that the Tribunal has not awarded compensation in accordance with law and facts and also the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
He further submits that the compensation awarded under all heads is on the lower side and sought for enhancement.
He also submits that the Tribunal has not awarded any amount towards future medical expenses.

10. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submitted that the Tribunal has passed the judgment and award in accordance with law and facts and there are no grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award.
He further submits that the Tribunal has awarded NC: 2023:KHC-D:9031-DB interest at the rate of 8% per annum which is on the higher side and sought for reduction in the interest rate to 6% per annum.
11. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties, the following points would arise for our consideration in these appeals?
(1) Whether the appellant-claimants have made out case for enhancement of compensation in these appeals?

5
(2) What order or award?

12. As regards Miscellaneous First Appeal No.102237 of 2020 which pertains to MVC No.472 of 2019 is concerned, the petitioner has produced Exhibit P7-wound certificate issued by the Government Hospital, Hagaribommanahalli which depicts that the injured has sustained CLW over right grater toe, abrasion over right side of forehead, blunt trauma over right femur, fracture of shaft of right tibia, soft tissue injury over right thigh and commuted compound fracture of right femur,
fracture of BB right leg.

Considering the evidence of treated Doctor and the multiple fractures as per Exhibits P9 to P13, the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9031-DB Tribunal has assessed the disability of the petitioner at 33% to the whole body and the same cannot be found fault with.
The petitioner has stated in his evidence that he was earning Rs.35,000/- per month by working as carpenter and also agriculture.
But he has not produced any documentary evidence to prove his income.
In the cases where income is not supported by documentary evidence, the notional income is to be taken.
As per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for the accidents of year 2018, the notional income is to be taken as Rs.11,750/- per month and the same is taken in this case.

The age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 29 years and as per the dictum of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of SARLA VERMA AND OTHERS v. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER reported in (2009)6 SCC 121, the applicable multiplier is 17.

entities.text: SARLA VERMA AND OTHERS v. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER reported in (2009)6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the evidence of Doctor-PW3, who has deposed that the injured has suffered 99% deformity to the limb, the Tribunal has taken rightly taken the disability at 33%, which cannot be found fault with.
Accordingly, the loss of future earning would be Rs.7,91,010/- (Rs.11,750/- x 12 x 17 x 33%).

Exhibits P9 to P18 reveals that the petitioner was admitted to Hospital for a span of eight months on several occasions for treatment as also follow-up treatment at SNR Hospital, Davanagere and Puttur Hospitals.
Hence, he is entitled for Rs.94,000/- under the head "loss of earning during laid-up period".
Considering discomforts the appellant should face through out the life-time, we deem it appropriate to award Rs.1,50,000/- under the head "loss of amenities".

As regards the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant regarding non-awarding of amount towards future medical expenses is concerned, we have carefully examined the evidence placed by the petitioner.
The petitioner has not whispered anything as to the future medical expenses.

However,
considering the nature of injuries, fractures suffered and operations undergone, as the implants are required to be removed which also require considerable expenses, we deem it appropriate to award Rs.50,000/- under the head "future medical expenses".

Accordingly, the compensation is awarded as follows:

7. Loss of future income 7,91,010  8. Loss of amenities and discomforts 1,50,000  9. Future Medical Expenses 50,000  Total 16,07,378 14.

As regards Miscellaneous First Appeal No.102238 of 2020 which is arising out of MVC No.473 of 2019 is concerned, the claimant has deposed that he has sustained various injuries which are evident from Exhibit P66-wound certificate issued by the Government Hospital, Hagaribommanahalli that the injured suffered lacerated wound over right knee and lateral side of below knee, right mid thigh, swelling and tenderness, so also sustained fracture of right femur.

With regard to disability,
PW3-treated Doctor has certified that the injured has suffered disability to the extent of 55% on examination of Doctor-PW3.
The Tribunal has rightly assessed the total disability at 18% to the whole body.
The age of the appellant as on the date of accident is 48 and hence, multiplier 13 is applicable.
The Tribunal has taken the notional income at Rs.8,000/- per month - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9031-DB which is not in consonance with the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
As per the guidelines, for the accidents of the year 2018, the notional income is fixed at Rs.11,750/-; accordingly, the same is taken in this case also.
Hence, the calculation for the loss of future earning will be (Rs.11,750/- x 12 x 13 x 18%)=Rs.3,29,940/-.

Considering the nature of injuries, period of hospitalization, etc., we intend to award the compensation under the following heads as follows:

7 2.
Travel expenses 15,000 3. Food and nourishment and attendant 15,000 charges
4. Loss of income during laid-up period 16,000 5.
Medical expenses 92,871 6.
Loss of future income 3,29,940 7.
Loss of amenities and discomforts 30,000

In the result, we pass the following:
ORDER 1. Both Appeals are allowed in part;
2. Judgment and award dated 11th June, 2020 passed in MVC.No.472 and 473 of 2019 by the Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9031-DB Tribunal-XIII at Hagaribommanahalli, are modified by enhancing the compensation to Rs.16,07,378 as against Rs.10,78,248/-; and to Rs.5,28,811 as against Rs.4,23,511/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
3.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation;
4. Respondent No.3-insurance company is directed to deposit the entire amount within 60 days from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment and award.
5. Registry shall draw award accordingly.

- 12 - Batageri Ramappa S/O. Hanumanthappa vs Mahesha @ Kalakappa S/O. Eranna Yemmi on 16 August, 2023
The Tribunal has taken the notional income at Rs.8,000/- per month - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9031-DB which is not in consonance with the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
As per the guidelines, for the accidents of the year 2018, the notional income is fixed at Rs.11,750/-; accordingly, the same is taken in this case also.
Hence, the calculation for the loss of future earning will be (Rs.11,750/- x 12 x 13 x 18%)=Rs.3,29,940/-.
Considering the nature of injuries, period of hospitalization, etc., we intend to award the compensation under the following heads as follows:
Amount Sl.No. Head (in Rs.)
1. Pain and agony 30,000 Batageri Ramappa S/O. Hanumanthappa vs Mahesha @ Kalakappa S/O. Eranna Yemmi on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109606509/
7 2.
Travel expenses 15,000 3. Food and nourishment and attendant 15,000 charges
4. Loss of income during laid-up period 16,000 5.
Medical expenses 92,871 6.
Loss of future income 3,29,940 7.
Loss of amenities and discomforts 30,000
Total 5,28,811
In the result, we pass the following:
ORDER 1. Both Appeals are allowed in part;
2. Judgment and award dated 11th June, 2020 passed in MVC.No.472 and 473 of 2019 by the Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9031-DB Tribunal-XIII at Hagaribommanahalli, are modified by enhancing the compensation to Rs.16,07,378 as against Rs.10,78,248/-; and to Rs.5,28,811 as against Rs.4,23,511/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
3.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation;
4. Respondent No.3-insurance company is directed to deposit the entire amount within 60 days from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment and award.
5. Registry shall draw award accordingly.
